text:
Hundreds of thousands of dollars in costs associated with Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding were covered by Umar Kremlev — a Russian businessman with close ties to Vladimir Putin and the head of his security detail, who leads the IBA, an organisation that for years was financially dependent on the state-owned company Gazprom. The payments were reportedly channelled through an IBA-linked entity in Dubai. These findings come from a ProPublica investigation.

WHAT PROPUBLICA FOUND

Based on financial documents and interviews with three people familiar with the organisation of the event, ProPublica reports that Kremlev covered a significant portion of the costs of the three-day wedding of Trump Jr. and Bettina Anderson in the Bahamas in May 2026. Among other expenses, he paid for the hire of the private island where the celebration took place and guests stayed, as well as a fireworks display; his staff were also reportedly involved in organising the event. The island alone can cost around $100,000 per night, while the company responsible for the fireworks charges around $70,000 for similar events.

The money was not reportedly paid directly from Kremlev’s private account. The payments were channelled through IB Challenger, a Dubai-based entity linked to the International Boxing Association. Minutes from subsequent IBA board meetings confirm that IB Challenger manages the organisation’s sponsorship contracts and supports the financing of its projects; the entity itself describes its role as that of a sports and marketing agency that secures funding for sporting organisations.

Kremlev’s press office told ProPublica that the IBA did not incur any expenses related to the wedding, but did not respond to questions about specific payments made by the Dubai-based entity. The source of the funds therefore remains unresolved.

GUESTS

The guest list numbered around 50 people, including Jared Kushner, Eric Trump and members of the newlyweds’ immediate families. Kremlev did not attend the ceremony itself — which, according to Trump Jr.’s spokesperson, had 18 guests — but arrived later with a larger group of Russians, reportedly taking some attendees by surprise.

The Russian group included, among others, Aleksandr Lagutin — who had previously held senior positions in a Russian defence company and a state-backed energy firm and who accompanied Kremlev during his visit to China — and Elena Sobol, one of Kremlev’s closest associates at the IBA. The Russian guests are virtually absent from photographs and videos later published by the Trump family.

THE KREMLEV–TRUMP JR. RELATIONSHIP

In September 2025, Trump Jr. appeared alongside Kremlev at an IBA forum in Istanbul. An official IBA statement described the two men as friends and announced further cooperation, stating explicitly that their ‘alliance will not remain symbolic’. Trump Jr. publicly praised Kremlev’s activities at the time.

A spokesperson for Trump Jr. did not dispute that Kremlev had provided funding. He said Kremlev was ‘a personal friend of Don’s’, not a business partner; they had met through a mutual acquaintance in the hunting community and became closer through their shared interest in boxing and outdoor activities. Kremlev’s office also described a ‘friendly relationship’ established ‘several years ago’. Kremlev maintains that he does not discuss politics with his American acquaintances, including Trump Jr.

KREMLEV, PUTIN AND THE FSO

▪️In April 2026, around a month before the wedding, Putin personally awarded Kremlev the Order of Friendship — as confirmed by the IBA’s official website. The organisation reported that Putin had praised its activities under Kremlev’s leadership. Kremlev had previously received a state award for his achievements in sport.

▪️Immediately before the wedding, Kremlev was in China during Putin’s visit. ProPublica, citing Chinese state media, reports that he was part of the group accompanying the Russian president; Kremlev’s office disputes the description of him as a member of the ‘official delegation’. The Ukrainian Main Intelligence Directorate (HUR) states that during Putin’s visit to China in 2023, Kremlev was a member of the official Russian delegation.

▪️The independent Russian outlet @wwwproektmedia established that Kremlev has for years been closely associated with Alexei Rubezhny, head of the Russian Presidential Security Service — a body within the FSO responsible, among other things, for Putin’s personal security. The two are said to have met through the pro-government Night Wolves motorcycle club, linked to Aleksandr ‘The Surgeon’ Zaldostanov and supported by the Kremlin for years. According to Proekt, it was Rubezhny who facilitated Kremlev’s rise to the leadership of the Russian Boxing Federation in 2016–2017.

▪️HUR describes Kremlev as a businessman and sports figure ‘close to Putin’ and a ‘close friend of the head of Putin’s security service’, and says that since 2016 he has led Russian boxing thanks to the support of the FSO leadership. This is the official position of the Ukrainian authorities, not an independent judicial finding.

IBA AND GAZPROM

Kremlev became president of the International Boxing Association in 2020, when the organisation was in the midst of a severe financial and reputational crisis.

Soon afterwards, he signed a sponsorship agreement with the state-controlled Gazprom, which the IBA officially presented as its ‘general partner’. IOC documents refer to a contract worth $50 million; the IOC concluded that the IBA had effectively become financially dependent on a single state-owned enterprise.

The status of this relationship after 2022 remains unclear. Kremlev claimed that the contract expired on 31 December 2022, and the IBA officially repeated this version. However, in December 2024, the IBA’s Secretary General and CEO, Chris Roberts, told The Guardian that the organisation was still receiving money from Gazprom and that ‘the Gazprom thing is still there’. In 2026, Kremlev’s office again told ProPublica that the agreement had ‘expired a long time ago’. People associated with the IBA, however, claim that the organisation’s funding still comes from Russia. At this stage, it cannot be stated with certainty that the money used for the wedding came directly from Gazprom; what is documented is the IBA’s previous dependence on Gazprom and the subsequent lack of transparency surrounding its funding.

In 2023, the IOC withdrew the IBA’s status as a recognised international federation, citing in its report, among other issues, governance failures, a lack of transparency regarding funding sources and a previous ‘effective dependence’ on a single Russian state-owned enterprise. The Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld the decision.

One former member of the IBA’s governing body told ProPublica that the IBA is ‘run by Putin’ and that sport serves as an instrument of Russian soft power. This is the source’s assessment; it does not constitute proof of a formal relationship of subordination.

BUSINESS AND SANCTIONS

The Proekt investigation describes how Kremlin-linked figures gained enormous influence over the Russian betting market: state mechanisms created a centralised betting-processing system used by entities connected to the Kremlin, and one of its companies became the operator of the state lottery. Proekt links these opportunities to Rubezhny’s patronage and Putin’s decisions. Kremlev himself has spoken publicly about the ‘unlimited opportunities’ Putin offers Russians. ProPublica also highlights the case of the Rolf dealership network: following the company’s nationalisation by the Russian authorities, Kremlev took control of it.

Kremlev has been subject to Ukrainian sanctions since 15 January 2023 — he is listed under number 182 in the annex to Sanctions Decree No. 23/2023, for a period of ten years, until January 2033. HUR justifies the sanctions by citing his close ties to Putin and the head of the Presidential Security Service, his support from the FSO in taking control of the Russian Boxing Federation, the relocation of the IBA’s operations to Russia, the suspension of the Ukrainian federation and the establishment of Gazprom as a key IBA sponsor.

Kremlev is not currently subject to any publicly available US sanctions.

ProPublica reports, citing a source close to the IBA’s leadership, that after 2022 he repeatedly feared being placed under US sanctions — in the context of the subsequent relocation of a significant portion of the IBA’s operations from Switzerland to the UAE and the expansion of its activities in the United States.

ProPublica also describes Kremlev’s involvement in the organisation ‘Healthy Fatherland’ (‘Здоровое Отечество’), led by his wife’s twin sister. HUR has included the organisation in a database of entities involved — according to the Ukrainian authorities — in the illegal deportation and forced displacement of Ukrainian citizens, including children, through programmes presented as ‘evacuation’, ‘rehabilitation’, leisure and education. The organisation did not respond to ProPublica’s questions. This is an allegation by the Ukrainian authorities, not a final court ruling against Kremlev.

WHAT HAS NOT BEEN ESTABLISHED

No evidence has been presented showing that Kremlev is a Russian intelligence officer or that the financing of the wedding constituted an operation by the Russian security services. ProPublica quotes former US counter-intelligence officials who note that Russian intelligence services often use money, gifts and personal relationships to gain access to influential figures; former NSC counter-intelligence director Holden Triplett said that money is a tried-and-tested method of gaining access. This is a counter-intelligence risk assessment, not evidence of a specific operation. ProPublica notes that it is not known whether Kremlev acted in coordination with the Russian state.

The question of motive also remains unanswered. According to Forbes estimates, Trump Jr. has a fortune worth hundreds of millions of dollars, meaning he did not need financial assistance to organise his wedding, while his acquaintance with Kremlev is relatively recent.

WHY THIS MATTERS

Donald Trump Jr. does not formally hold a position in the administration, but he plays a significant political role within his father’s inner circle and has, among other things, been involved in the process of selecting personnel for the administration. Jared Kushner, who is involved in the US administration’s negotiations concerning Russia and Ukraine, attended the wedding. ProPublica presents the financing of the event primarily as a potential issue of access and influence rather than as a proven political transaction.

The documented chain is therefore narrower than some media headlines suggest: the Kremlin → long-standing close ties with Putin’s head of security and the FSO → promotion within Russian sport → IBA funding by Gazprom → personal contacts with Putin and state honours → contacts with Trump Jr. → hundreds of thousands of dollars spent on the US president’s son’s private wedding.

text:
Long term thinking for as basic and obvious as it sounds probably triumphs all other golden rules in life, except maybe adaptability. 
It still comes before adapability, anyway.

People act like other people who tell them this stuff are expecting them to know the unknown, and then plan a future around that. But it's not about the unknown, first and foremost. It's about what is known, first. I know what I care about today and have cared about the last few years, what I've built and what I always seem to default back to thinking about. And unlike people or events, those can be controlled to eventually influence the unknown to some degree afterwards.

There is the cliche example of going to the gym so you get healthier, but that's still in its own way planning around the unknown since you don't know if you'll loosen your discs in your back, if some guy has a bad day and hits you with a barbell, or if a freak accident happens without a spotter. My point? It's a cliche example with those being the possibilities for the unknown, but nobody will typically use this as an excuse to not go to the gym because it's paranoid beyond a reasonable absurdity. Yet it's still true, but you won't go unknown first, known after on this one.

The same logic applies here. A gym routine becomes a habit, a habit is maintained at first through discipline then it becomes autopilot, yet this logic never gets applied to the other equally if not more so mundane moments in life. Just me laying here and typing this on the fly as it comes, just pushing myself past thoughts that ultimately don't matter in favor of the ones that do matter, a type of mental discipline that even guys in the army forgo, yet Buddhist monks have effortless ease and control, yet useless application of outside the spiritual realm.

You could probably make an argument for stoicism here, but stoicism still enforces repression of the emotions and doesn't account for when life gets a reaction out of you that is inevitably expected. As a stoic, you'll find your emotions still governing your unconscious mind in ways you aren't equipped with stoicism to repair. Ironically, a faith in God will cover this part, but even faith is said to not pay the bills. Faith's role also isn't exactly defined past the unconscious collective and spiritual connection. 

Instead, seek the most immediate thing in your environment: People.

They're all really just walking full body mirrors of your own time on earth, anyway. You always end back in circles to them one way or another, you always take the worst of your trauma, and your highest highs through them, your evolution as a human was to take advantage of them and to gimp you for isolation, and it's easily the thing society is always at odds with and formed every single thing both good and bad around. People. At the center of it all, is people, and you're always going to see people yip like dogs when they are scorched by the village, then behave as if they are the fire when the village offers them wood and worships them. There is no bigger hypocrite than somebody who is alive, because even a man alone in the woods or a lone monk still lives on the subsidies and subsistence of other... people.

Learn to embrace that. That's the long term. Reflections inevitably bounce your light back. That light is shared. Let there be light.

text:
since many of you have been asking, here’s what #SeaOfNoReturn is actually about:

it’s a historical romance. a border prince's son wanders somewhere he shouldn't, a child princess passes by, the moment means nothing to her but everything to him. his clan is forbidden by law from marrying a princess, so marrying her is the only door into the palace that will ever open for someone like him. she, meanwhile, grows up motherless and fatherless in a place where an orange has a correct way to be peeled, where she is a rank before she is a girl. she marries him not knowing she's a move on someone else's board. she builds a wall around herself bc she's spent her whole life learning that survival means never fully belonging to anyone. he spends years dismantling it, stone by stone, and it works. she lets herself believe he could be home. she only asks him for one thing: don't destroy the state (her brother’s state) to get what you want. he smiles and promises but privately decides he doesn't have to choose, that he can keep her and the army waiting in the south, that a child will eventually teach her which one matters more. when his ambition finally becomes an open war, she refuses to live as the ornament of the man burning down her family's house. she also loses a child in the crossfire of a war he started. she's offered a future, a seat beside the new power, safety and she answers with the one act that is entirely hers: she swallows the golden seal of her own rank so that the last thing inside her is the name of the house she was born to, not the one she married into. she stays his wife in the history books but refuses, in the end, to be buried beside him. he only understands what he did once she's gone. he moves crabapple trees to face a grave toward the sea. he waits at the place where the old stories say lovers find each other again. but when he finally dies too, she isn't there. she was never going to be.

@BIG_SGT_D — “🇻🇦 The people of the prince who is to come (Dan 9:26)” over a 6-panel collage of Luther, Spurgeon, Froom, Huss, Cranmer, and Wycliffe calling the Pope/Rome Antichrist or Babylon.

Dan 9:26 names the people who destroy Jerusalem and the sanctuary after Messiah is cut off — historically Titus’s Roman army in AD 70. Those were pagan imperial troops, not the Catholic Church.

1. Equivocation — “Rome” the pagan army that razed the Temple is treated as “Rome” the later Catholic Church.

2. Anachronism — A 1st-c. military destruction is projected onto a later Christian institution that was not that army.

3. Appeal to authority — Six selected voices calling the Pope Antichrist are stacked as if they settle what Daniel meant.

4. Cherry-picking — Only writers already committed to papal-antichrist polemic; omits the standard reading (Titus) and any contrary exegesis.

5. Non sequitur — Reformers denouncing the papacy does not make Dan 9:26 identify the Vatican.

6. Begging the question — Assumes Pope = Antichrist, then captions the verse as if it already names the Vatican.

7. Guilt by association — Same city name (Rome) is treated as the same “people.”

8. Hasty generalization — Six hostile quotes become proof the whole Catholic Church is the people of Dan 9:26.

9. Loaded language — Vatican emoji + Antichrist / Babylon / “mother of harlots” / “mountain of rubbish” replace an argument from the text.

10. Ambiguity — Treats a contested verse (prince = Titus? Messiah? future figure?) as if the Vatican reading were the plain sense.

11. Composition — What is said of pagan Rome, or of some popes, is applied to the entire Church as Daniel’s destroyers.

12. Proof by juxtaposition — Flag + verse + quote collage is offered as identification; no actual exegesis of Daniel 9.

If Congress could appreciate the government when it does something right, offer better alternatives, and focus on making #IndiaBetter instead of condemning every decision of @BJP4India, I would be the first to admit that India finally has a strong and constructive opposition.

And frankly, constantly invoking the Nehru-Gandhi family's history, personal tragedies and Sonia Gandhi's foreign-origin background to build political narratives does not convince my generation anymore. We want policies, solutions, accountability and results—not emotional vote-bank politics.

At one of @RahulGandhi's conferences/roadshows, he spoke about women being unsafe.

As a woman, I have a very different lived experience.

I feel more empowered today than I did before 2014. I can speak about my rights, question decisions and fight for what I believe is right.

I still remember being told that I could not join the #NDA simply because I was a girl.

Today, I am a successful Army officer.

But getting here was not easy. I had to fight many battles—socially, professionally and personally—to prove that being a woman was never a limitation.

So when politicians speak about women's empowerment, I don't judge them by speeches. I judge them by whether women actually get the freedom, opportunity and confidence to break barriers.

My generation has lived through those battles.

That is why you can appreciate good work across party lines and still understand why many of us remain deeply sceptical of #Congress .

**Give us solutions. Give us an alternative. Give us a reason to trust you—not just another reason to dislike the #BJP .**

text:
John Dickinson, 'Pen Man of the Patriots/Revolution" & his warnings of corporate tyranny

Corporate tyranny, is not something one hears as part public debate, the 250 year celebrations or a reason for rebellion
 (from google AI-mode)
@grok>
John Dickinson, famously nicknamed the "Penman of the Patriots" (or "Penman of the Revolution"), wrote passionately against the East India Company primarily in his late 1773 series titled Letters from the Country (specifically the second letter). Writing under the pseudonym "A Countryman," Dickinson targeted the company following the passage of the 1773 Tea Act.

His writings against the East India Company focused on several key arguments:
•Exposing Corporate Tyranny: Dickinson explicitly connected British imperial policy to the East India Company's brutal corporate behavior in India, warning Americans that a commercial empire is not a peaceful one. 

•Highlighting Atrocities: He fiercely criticized the company's track record abroad, writing that they had "levied war, incited rebellions, dethroned lawful princes, and sacrificed millions for the sake of gain".

•Condemning Monopolies: He detailed how the company used "the most unparalleled barbarities, extortions, and monopolies" to achieve its goals. 

•Warning of Colonial Ruin: Dickinson argued that the Tea Act was designed to bail out the company and establish a monopoly in America, allowing them to "hope to repair their broken fortunes by the ruin of American freedom and liberty!" 

These essays built upon the constitutional arguments he pioneered years earlier in his highly influential Letters from a Farmer in Pennsylvania (1767–1768), turning public sentiment firmly against both British taxation and corporate overreach.
<...>

John Dickinson was deeply horrified by the 1770 Bengal Famine, and he explicitly used it as a terrifying warning of what would be unleashed on the 13 American colonies if the East India Company was allowed to establish its foothold through the 1773 Tea Act. 

The Famine as an Engineered Atrocity
In his late 1773 series, Letters from the Country (penned under the pseudonym "A Countryman"), Dickinson recounted the horrors of the Great Bengal Famine, which killed an estimated 10 million people—roughly one-third of the region's population. Crucially, Dickinson argued that this starvation was not a natural disaster, but an artificial crisis engineered by corporate greed

He wrote of the East India Company: 

"Fifteen hundred Thousand, it is said, perished by Famine in one Year, not because the Earth denied its Fruits, but this Company and its Servants engrossed all the Necessities of Life, and set them at so high a Rate, that the Poor could not purchase them." 

The Fear: America as the Next "Theatre of Rapine"
Dickinson’s primary goal was to wake up the American colonists to the true nature of the enemy at their doorstep. He warned that the the East India Company, having fully bled the Indian subcontinent dry, were now turning their insatiable corporate apparatus toward North America

He warned that after subjugating India, the Company would now: 

"...cast their Eyes on America, as a new Theatre, whereon to exercise their Talents of Rapine, Oppression and Cruelty." 

Why Dickinson Argued the Tea Act Was a Trap

Dickinson explained to his fellow colonists that the seemingly cheap tea offered by the Tea Act was a trojan horse. If the colonists purchased the tea, they would simultaneously: 
1Bail out a corrupt corporation: Provide financial relief to a bankrupt, tyrannical monopoly that had devastated Bengal.
2Accept the precedent of parliamentary taxation: Relinquish their constitutional right to self-governance
3Invite corporate tyranny to American shores: Allow a company governed by "avarice" and "unparalleled barbarities" to gradually monopolize American trade, leaving the 13 colonies vulnerable to the same artificial scarcities, heavy-handed tax extractions, & absolute ruin that had broken India<

You are just biased and politically slanted. You chased the approval of the international media, but in truth you are nothing but traitors to your own country. The points below are irrefutable, but you are not ready for that conversation:

**Israel, Asymmetry, and Narrative Inversion**

Israel is, in the institutionally relevant sense — universal suffrage for citizens, competitive elections, genuine alternation in office, a legal opposition, an adversarial press, and a judiciary able to constrain the executive — the only functioning democracy in the Middle East.¹ Neighboring regimes are absolute monarchies, hereditary autocracies, or systems in which the ballot, when it exists, does not change who holds power. The contrast does not erase Israel’s internal strains (fragile coalitions, the judicialization of politics, the status of the Arab-Israeli minority, and the problem of occupation). It does, however, rule out any equivalence with Damascus, Tehran, Hamas-run Gaza, or Riyadh.

The difference is not merely electoral. In Israel, women, gay people, and religious or ethnic minorities possess, as a matter of positive law, the same civil and political rights as other citizens: they vote, stand for office, petition the courts, serve in the Israel Defense Forces, and sit on the Supreme Court and in the cabinet. Public life does not criminalize sexual orientation, nor does it reduce women to permanent legal guardianship. In neighboring Islamic states governed in whole or in part by Sharia — Iran, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Hamas-controlled Gaza, and, to varying degrees, Jordan, Egypt, and the Palestinian Authority — the picture is different: criminalization of homosexuality, male guardianship, unequal inheritance and testimony, and apostasy and blasphemy as penal offenses. Anyone who equates “human rights in the Levant” without this distinction substitutes geography for law.⁶

The asymmetry of movement is related. Israel has repeatedly admitted Arabs from neighboring countries for work, medical treatment and, in certain periods, trade and tourism. The reverse is almost never true: an Israeli passport, especially a Jewish one, is barred in most states of the Arab League and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). Those who speak of a “regional apartheid” usually omit this elementary fact of entry rights.

The territorial imbalance is still sharper. Israel covers about 22,000 km². The 57 OIC members together cover on the order of 31.6 million km². Israel is roughly 0.07 percent of that area — about 1,435 times smaller than the whole.² The rhetoric of a “colonial giant” collides with geography.

In the conduct of war, the moral asymmetry is not identical to the territorial one, but it is observable. Israel operates with prior warnings, corridors, tactical pauses, and guided munitions because the domestic political cost of every civilian death is high. Hamas, Hezbollah, and associated militias do the opposite: they embed combat assets in hospitals, schools, and dense urban fabric. Using one’s own population — especially women and children — as a deterrent is not a tactical accident; it is a documented pattern in military, journalistic, and, in part, Hamas’s own sources.³ When an attack hits an Israeli soldier or civilian, public celebration is not a deviation: it is political liturgy.

The rejection of partition is not a recent legend either. At Camp David (July 2000) and in the Clinton Parameters (December 2000), a formula was mediated that contemplated a Palestinian state, a capital in East Jerusalem, and most of the West Bank, with land swaps. Ehud Barak accepted the parameters; Yasser Arafat did not close the deal. Clinton later called the refusal a historic error: Arafat “could not bring himself to say yes.”⁴ Palestinian historiography and part of the American revisionist literature insist there was no formal written offer and that the details (refugees, sovereignty over the Haram al-Sharif/Temple Mount, contiguity) were insufficient. The political fact remains: there was a window for statehood in exchange for an end to the conflict, and it was not taken. What was reiterated, in founding charters and in sermons, was not merely a claim about borders, but the permanent illegitimacy of Israel as a Jewish state.

October 7, 2023, does not belong to the category of “resistance” in the classical sense of the law of peoples. It was a deliberate massacre of civilians — murder, rape, arson, abduction, and audiovisual recording for humiliation. The subsequent marketing by sectors of the Western left and of political Islam inverted the causal sequence: the aggressor becomes the inaugural victim, the state that responds becomes the structural perpetrator, and the crime disappears under the fog of “context.” Inverting the facts is not a communications accident; it is a method.

The charge of genocide collides with the long-run demographic series. On UN estimates for the West Bank and Gaza (“State of Palestine”), the population rose from about 945,000 in 1950 to on the order of 5.4–5.6 million in 2024–2025 — growth of roughly 470–490 percent, nearly sixfold in seventy-five years.⁵ War kills; the criminal type of genocide requires intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a group as such. A people that multiplies several times over on the same territory across three-quarters of a century has not been “erased.” The recent contraction in Gaza after 2023 is real and grave and must be recorded; it does not rewrite the secular trajectory.

The civilizational contrast in outcomes is equally stark and, in large measure, independent of the rhetoric of “occupation.” Israel, with scant territory and under permanent threat, concentrates Nobel Prizes, patents, pharmaceuticals, agritech, and dual-use technology the world uses. The Palestinian Authority and Hamas have, over decades, received large volumes of international aid. A substantial share evaporated into clientelism, leaders’ estates, and arsenals. The difference in output is not explained by movement restrictions alone; it is explained by what is done with capital, with schools, and with the idea of a future.

The concluding formula is old because it is structural. If Palestinian organizations laid down their arms and accepted Israel as a permanent fact, there would be room — narrow, difficult, but real — for a political accommodation. If Israel laid down its arms, it would cease to exist as a political community. That is not a metaphor. It is the program, still written into documents and sermons, of eliminating the Jewish state — not of merely correcting a line on the map.

---

**Notes**

1. Freedom House has classified Israel as “Free” in the region continuously since the 1970s; the *Economist* Democracy Index treats it as a “flawed democracy,” a category it virtually occupies alone in the Middle East alongside Cyprus. Critiques of “ethnocracy” (Yiftachel and others) refer mainly to the nexus of the Jewish state, the Arab minority, and the territories. They do not equate Israel with a one-party regime.

2. Israel’s usually cited area: ~20,770–22,072 km², depending on whether the Golan and East Jerusalem are included. Aggregate OIC area: ~31.6 million km² (SESRIC yearbooks). 22,000 / 31,600,000 ≈ 0.07%; 31,600,000 / 22,000 ≈ 1,436.

3. IDF accounts, urban-warfare analyses (John Spencer and others), and dossiers on tunnels under civilian facilities document the pattern. Human-rights organizations contest that every operation in a inhabited area constitutes a “human shield” in the strict sense of IHL. The distinction matters legally; it does not erase the deliberate militarization of Gaza’s civilian fabric.

4. Bill Clinton, *My Life*, and later remarks (Georgetown, 2014): Barak accepted the parameters; Arafat did not. Clayton Swisher and IMEU contest the “generous offer” narrative. The disagreement is over the density of the offer, not over the absence of a window for statehood.

5. UNDESA / Macrotrends: 944,807 (1950) and about 5.49 million (2024) for the West Bank + Gaza aggregate. PCBS estimates ~5.56 million at the end of 2025, with a sharp drop in Gaza after the war. The demographic argument refutes the loose use of “genocide”; it is not a moral discharge of civilian casualties in 2023–2026.

6. In Israel, the formal equality of women and the non-criminalization of homosexuality coexist with real tensions: ultra-Orthodox communities, draft exemptions, and residual social discrimination. That is a different order of problem from the criminalization of sodomy, male guardianship (*wilaya*), *hudud* courts, and execution for apostasy. Arab Israelis vote and sit in the Knesset; in Gaza and in most Sharia-governed neighbors, the equivalent space does not exist.

THE SONS OF THE SERPENT TRIBE
OPHIOLATREIA

Original Title Page from FIRST (& Only Original) Edition

D. OPHIOLATREIA
THE following comes from Chapter 1 of Ophiolatreia, anonymously written by Hargrave Jennings:

In Egypt was a serpent named Thermuthis, which was looked upon as very sacred; and the natives are said to have made use of it as a royal tiara, with which they ornamented the statues of Isis. We learn from Diodorus Siculus that the kings of Egypt wore high bonnets, which terminated in a round ball, and the whole was surrounded by figures of asps. The priests, likewise, upon their bonnets had the representation of serpents. The ancients had a notion that when Saturn devoured his own children, his wife Ops deceived him by substituting a large stone in lieu of one of his sons, which stone was called Abadir. But Ops and Opis, represented here as a feminine, was the serpent deity, and Abadir is the same personage under a different denomination. Abadir seems to be a variation of Ob-Adur, and signifies the serpent god Orus. One of these stones, which Saturn was supposed to have swallowed instead of a child, stood, according to Pausanias, at Delphi. It was esteemed very sacred, and used to have libations of wine poured upon it daily; and upon festivals was otherwise honoured. The purport of the above was probably this: it was for a long time a custom to offer children at the altar of Saturn; but in process of time they removed it, and in its room erected a stone pillar, before which they made their vows, and offered sacrifices of another nature. This stone which they thus substituted was called Ab-Adar, from the deity represented by it. The term Ab generally signifies a father, but in this instance it certainly relates to a serpent, which was indifferently styled Ab, Aub, and Ob. Some regard Abadon, or, as it is mentioned in the Book of the Revelation, Abaddon, to have been the name of the same Ophite god, with whose worship the world had been so long infected. He is termed Abaddon, the angel of the bottomless pit - the prince of darkness. In another place he is described as the dragon, that old serpent, which is the devil, and Satan. Hence the learned Heinsius is supposed to be right in the opinion which he has given upon this passage, when he makes Abaddon the same as the serpent Pytho.

It is said that in the ritual of Zoroaster the great expanse of the heavens, and even nature itself, was described under the symbol of a serpent. [Note: Eusebius.] The like was mentioned in the Octateuch of Ostanes; and moreover, in Persia and in other parts of the East they erected temples to the serpent tribe, and held festivals to their honour, esteeming them the supreme of all Gods, and the superintendants of the whole world. The worship began among the people of Chaldea. They built the city Opis upon the Tigris, and were greatly addicted to divination and to the worship of the serpent. From Chaldea the worship passed into Egypt, where the serpent deity was called Canoph, Caneph, and C'neph. It had also the name of Ob, or Oub, and was the same as the Basilicus, or Royal Serpent; the same also as the Thermuthis, and in like manner was made use of by way of ornament to the statues of their Gods. The chief Deity of Egypt is said to have been Vulcan, who was also styled Opas, as we learn from Cicero. He was the same as Osiris, the Sun; and hence was often called Ob-El, or Pytho-Sol; and there were pillars sacred to him, with curious hieroglyphical inscriptions, which had the same name. They were very lofty, and narrow in comparison of their length; hence among the Greeks, who copied from the Egyptians, everything gradually tapering to a point was styled Obelos, and Obeliscus. Ophel (Oph-El) was a name of the same purport, and many sacred mounds, or Tapha, were thus denominated from the serpent Deity, to whom they were sacred.

Sanchoniathon makes mention of a history which he once wrote upon the worship of the serpent. The title of this work, according to Eusebius, was Ethothion, or Ethothia. Another treatise upon the same subject was written by Pherecydes Tyrus, which was probably a copy of the former; for he is said to have composed it from some previous accounts of the Phoenicians. The title of his book was the Theology of Ophion, styled Ophioneus, and his worshippers were called Ophionidae. Thoth and Athoth were certainly titles of the Deity in the Gentile world; and the book of Sanchoniathon might very possibly have been from hence named Ethothion, or more truly, Athothion. But, from the subject upon which it was written, as well as from the treatise of Pherecydes, we have reason to think that Athothion, or Ethothion, was a mistake for Ath-Ophion, a title which more immediately related to that worship of which the writer treated. Ath was a sacred title, as we have shewn, and we imagine that this dissertation did not barely relate to the serpentine Deity, but contained accounts of his votaries, the Ophites, the principal of which were the sons of Chus. The worship of the serpent began among them, and they were from thence denominated Ethiopians, and Aithopians, which the Greeks rendered Aithiopes. They did not receive this name from their complexion, as has sometimes been surmised, for the branch of Phut and the Luhim, were probably of a deeper dye; but they were most likely so called from Ath-Ope, and Ath-Opis, the God which they worshipped. This may be shewn from Pliny. He says that the country Ethiopia (and consequently the people), had the name of Aethiop, from a personage who was a Deity - ob Aethiope Vulcani filio. The Aethiopes brought these rites into Greece, and called the island where they first established them Ellopia, Solis Serpentis insula. It was the same as Euboea, a name of the like purport, in which island was a region named Ethiopium. Euboea is properly Oub-Aia, and signifies, the Serpent Island. The same worship prevailed among the Hyperboreans, as we may judge from the names of the sacred women who used to come annually to Delos; they were priestesses of the Tauric Goddess. Hercules was esteemed the chief God, the same as Chronus, and was said to have produced the Mundane egg. He was represented in the Orphic theology under the mixed symbol of a lion and a serpent, and sometimes of a serpent only.

The Cuthites, under the title of Heliadae, having settled at Rhodes, as they were Hivites, or Ophites, the island was in consequence named Ophiusa. There was likewise a tradition that it had once swarmed with serpents. (Bochart says the island is said to have been named Rhodus from Rhad, a Syriac word for a serpent). The like notion prevailed almost in every place where they settled. They came under the more general titles of Leleges and Pelasgi; but more particularly of Elopians, Europians, Oropians, Asopians, Inopians, Ophionians, and Aethiopes, as appears from the names which they bequeathed; and in most places where they resided there were handed down traditions which alluded to their original title of Ophites. In Phrygia, and upon the Hellespont, whither they sent out colonies very early, was a people styled the Ophiogeneis, or the serpent breed, who were said to retain an affinity and correspondence with serpents; and a notion prevailed that some hero, who had conducted them, was changed from a serpent to a man. In Colchis was a river Ophis, and there was another of the same name in Arcadia. It was so named from a body of people who settled upon its banks, and were said to have been conducted by a serpent.

It is said these reptiles are seldom found in islands, but that Tenos, one of the Cyclades, was supposed to have once swarmed with them. [Note: Aristoph.]

Thucydides mentions a people of Aetotia, called Ophionians; and the temple of Apollo at Petara, in Lycia, seems to have had its first institution from a priestess of the same name. The island of Cyprus was called Ophiusa, and Ophiodes, from the serpents with which it was supposed to have abounded. Of what species they were is nowhere mentioned, excepting only that about Paphos there was said to have been a kind of serpent with two legs. By this is meant the Ophite race, who came from Egypt, and from Syria, and got footing in this island. They settled also in Crete, where they increased greatly in numbers; so that Minos was said by an unseemly allegory, opheis ouresai, serpentes, minxisse. The island Seriphus was one vast rock, by the Romans called saxum seriphium, and made use of as a large kind of prison for banished persons. It is represented as having once abounded with serpents, and it is styled by Virgil, serpentifera, as the passage is corrected by Scaliger.

It is said by the Greeks that Medusa's head was brought by Perseus; by this is meant the serpent Deity, whose worship was here introduced by people called Peresians. Medusa's head denoted divine wisdom, and the island was sacred to the serpent, as is apparent from its name. The Athenians were esteemed Serpentiginae, and they had a tradition that the chief guardian of their Acropolis was a serpent.

It is reported of the goddess Ceres that she placed a dragon for a guardian to her temple at Eleusis, and appointed another to attend upon Erectheus. Aegeus of Athens, according to Androtion, was of the serpent breed, and the first king of the country is said to have been a dragon. Others make Cecrops the first who reigned. He is said to have been of a two-fold nature, being formed with the body of a man blended with that of a serpent.

Diodorus says that this was a circumstance deemed by the Athenians inexplicable; yet he labours to explain it by representing Cecrops as half a man and half a brute, because he had been of two different communities. Eustathius likewise tries to solve it nearly upon the same principles, and with the like success. Some have said of Cecrops that he underwent a metamorphosis, being changed from a serpent to a man. By this was meant, according to Eustathius, that Cecrops by coming into Hellas divested himself of all the rudeness and barbarity of his country, and became more civilised and human. This is declared by some to be too high a compliment to be paid to Greece in its infant state, and detracts greatly from the character of the Egyptians. The learned Marsham therefore animadverts with great justice, "it is more probable that he introduced into Greece the urbanity of his own country, than that he was beholden to Greece for anything from thence." In respect to the mixed character of this personage, we may easily account for it. Cecrops was certainly a title of the Deity, who was worshipped under this emblem. Something of the like nature was mentioned of Triptolemus and Erichtonius, and the like has been said of Hercules. The natives of Thebes in Boeotia, like the Athenians, esteemed themselves of the serpent race. The Lacedaemonians likewise referred themselves to the same original. Their city is said of old to have swarmed with serpents. The same is said of the city Amyelae in Italy, which was of Spartan origin. They came hither in such abundance that it was abandoned by the inhabitants. Argos was infested in the same manner till Apis came from Egypt and settled in that city. He was a prophet, the reputed son of Apollo, anda person of great skill and sagacity, and to him they attributed the blessing of having their country freed from this evil. Thus the Argives gave the credit to this imaginary personage of clearing their land of this grievance, but the brood came from the very quarter from whence Apis was supposed to have arrived. They were certainly Hivites from Egypt, and the same story is told of that country. It is represented as having been of old over-run with serpents, and almost depopulated through their numbers. Diodorus Siculus seems to understand this literally, but a region that was annually overflowed, and that too for so long a season, could not well be liable to such a calamity. They were serpents of another nature with which it was thus infested, and the history relates to the Cuthites, the original Ophitae, who for a long time possessed that country. They passed from Egypt to Syria, and to the Euphrates, and mention is made of a particular breed of serpents upon that river, which were harmless to the natives but fatal to anybody else. This can hardly be taken literally; for whatever may be the wisdom of the serpent it cannot be sufficient to make these distinctions. These serpents were of the same nature as the birds of Diomedes, and the dogs in the temple of Vulcan; and the histories relate to Ophite priests, who used to spare their own people and sacrifice strangers, a custom which prevailed at one time in most parts of the world. The Cuthite priests are said to have been very learned; and, as they were Ophites, whoever had the advantage of their information was said to have been instructed by serpents.

As the worship of the serpent was of old so prevalent, many places, as well as people, from thence received their names. Those who settled in Campania were called Opici, which some would have changed to Ophici, because they were denominated from serpents. They are in reality both names of the same purport, and denote the origin of the people.

We meet with places called Opis, Ophis, Ophitaea, Ophionia, Ophioessa, Ophiodes, and Ophiusa. This last was an ancient name by which, according to Stephanus, the islands Rhodes, Cynthus, Besbicus, Tenos, and the whole continent of Africa, were distinguished. There were also cities so-called. Add to these places denominated Oboth, Obona, and reversed, Onoba, from Ob, which was of the same purport.

Clemens Alexandrinus says that the term Eva signified a serpent if pronounced with a proper aspirate, and Epiphanius says the same thing. We find that there were places of this name. There was a city Eva in Arcadia, and another in Macedonia. There was also a mountain Eva, or Evan, taken notice of by Pausanias, between which and Ithome lay the city Messene. He mentions also an Eva in Argolis, and speaks of it as a large town. Another name for a serpent, which we have not yet noticed, was Patan, or Pitan. Many places in different parts were denominated from this term. Among others was a city in Laconia, and another in Mysia, which Stephanus styles a city of Aeolia. They were undoubtedly so named from the worship of the serpent, Pitan, and had probably Dracontia, which were figures and devices relative to the religion which prevailed. Ovid mentions the latter city, and has some allusions to its ancient history when he describes Medea as flying through the air from Athea to Colchis. The city was situate upon the ruin Eva, or Evan, which the Greeks rendered Evenus. According to Strabo it is compounded of Eve-Ain, the fountain or river of Eva the serpent.

It is remarkable that the Opici, who are said to have been named from serpents, had also the name of Pitanatae; at least, one part of that family was so-called. Pitanatae is a term of the same purport as Opici, and relates to the votaries of Pitan, the serpent Deity, which was adored by that people. Menelaus was of old called Pitanates, as we learn from Hesychius, and the reason of it may be known from his being a Spartan, by which he was intimated one of the Serpentigenae, or Ophites. Hence he was represented with a serpent for a device upon his shield. It is said that a brigade, or portion of infantry, was among some of the Greeks named Pitanates, and the soldiers in consequence of it must have been termed Pitanatae, undoubtedly, because they had the Pitan, or serpent, for their standard. Analogous to this, among other nations there were soldiers called Draconarii. In most countries the military standard was an emblem of the Deity there worshipped.

What has already been said has thrown some light upon the history of this primitive idolatry, and we have shewn that wherever any of these Ophite colonies settled, they left behind from their rites and institutions, as well as from the names which they bequeathed to places, ample memorials, by which they may be clearly traced out.
- Ophiolatreia, pp. 3-9.

E. COMMENTS
There are many themes presented above, which we have come across previously. We think it fair to say that the Serpent Breed, or Serpent Tribe, is none other than the human offspring and/or incarnations of the Anunnaki. Let us assume for a moment that what we have just quoted above is a work of True History. That is, if True ESOTERIC History. Even today, we know precious little about what actually happened in the past, especially in the past of, say, 3000 years ago. We know that several kingdoms existed, such as Babylonia, Egypt, India, Phoenicia, and other places existed. But - how did the Esoteric Cultus survive, from the days of Sumer, to today? And what is to account for the conscious memory of Humankind suddenly coming to life in the 7th - 6th centuries B.C.E.?

This lengthy extract is basically a short account of what General Forlong devotes 230 pages in volume one of his excellent survey, Rivers of Life: to Tree and Serpent Worship.

Some of these things can be plotted on the map, and on the historical timeline. Perhaps a great deal is fabulous, or at the least is "myth" - history turned into fiction for certain people of today to regard as bunk. Well, we do not regard any of it as bunk.

One of the main strands of the story is given in this extract - that of the Aethiopes. We have come across traces of this story in several different places. In fact, we can see a story that goes back to the destruction of Sumer, to the migrations that followed that destruction, and to a survival of various cults in the region to the North and West of India.

Eventually, some of these Priests are exiled and come across, by way of the Island of the Dioscuri - Socotra. Some travel up the Incense Route, and end up in the Nabatean regions and in Palestine. Some go across to Ethiopia, and from there to Egypt. By the time the Priesthood of the Solis Serpentis reaches Egypt, we are getting close to the time of Akhnaten. After the demise of Akhnaten, and his religion, some of our Priests migrate north, and across the Mediterranean, to Euboea. We can take it from there in the next extract, below, from the Dionysian Artificers, by Da Costa.

It is necessary to go into the past, beyond the birth of the Gnosis, to the Near-Eastern Serpent Cults, and to the Mystery Traditions, and perhaps to the oldest cults we can find traces of, in order to view the Current as a continuous whole, a continuity as complete as the Ouroboros itself.

F. ORIGINS OF SERPENT GODS
Zecharia Sitchin points out that EnKi was given Africa, while EnLil had Mesopotamia, Inanna the Indus Valley, and NinHarsag the Sinai Peninsula. Notice that the Ethiopians, according to Jennings, were called the sons of Vulcan. This is the same appellation given to Adapa and Enmeduranki. Vulcan is none other than Ptah, who is none other than EnKi, according to popular syncretization. Interestingly, Im-Hetep, or Imouthis, is given as Ptah's son, in the Memphite Triad. Imouthis is also known as Asklepios, who is also known as Agathodaimon. Also, I-M-Hetep is known as the first important builder in Egyptian history, as well as being a physician. Interesting.

Also, the Cuthites may be like the Cuthans, mentioned above, but they are also confused with the Cushites, or sons of Cush. The Cushites came from the Land of Cush, which is known to be Nubia and Ethiopia.

It is stated that these Cuthites migrated from Egypt, to Syria, to the Euphrates. Also it is said that the Aith-Opes or Ethiopians migrated to Greece, and brought the rites of Serpent worship with them. Also, in connection with this it is said that Erectheus is the individual responsible for bringing the rites of Eleusis to Greece, to Athens. Now, could these Cuthites be connected with the Babylonian Priests we have spoken of, i.e., the Nergals of Cutha? Perhaps. We know that about 43 miles north of Baghdad on the west bank of the Tigris river is the location of the ancient city of Opis, where at least two crucial events took place. First, this is where the Persians, under the command of Cyrus, overthrew Babylon and claimed the whole area as a satrapy. Second, this is where Alexander the Great was said to have invited dignitaries from all over his empire for the purpose of feasting and so that he could consolidate them all together and proclaim his New World Order.

As can be seen, these legendary stories may not be so legendary after all. Competent scholars are confirming the legends bit by bit, even if they would regard these legends as little more than fictions. The work we just quoted above may not have been written by an expert academician of high repute, whatever that is supposed to indicate, but Brother Jennings was an Adept of high repute, and drew from a wide variety of classical sources, some of which not everybody has access to, especially today. The fact that a High Initiate wrote the above really should be no bar to its believability, or to its credibility.

Interested parties (that is, those with agendas) including some Freemasons in the mix, as well as their opponents continue to prefer denial of all stories of the past which conflict with their preconceived notions. It is safer to assume that the Craft is somehow attached to the craft guilds of the 17th century and became Freemasonry in 1717. It is safer to relegate history to something else, far removed from our own roots.

For those of us in whom the Historical Tradition is The Path, and that by which we HAVE Attained much, this is all rather ludicrous. That which is still condemned today as heresy, perhaps should be condemned as heresy, or as false, in order to keep out the riff raff. Yet, our ancestors practiced the same way as we do now, and when we are condemned as heretics, we can point to our traditional lineage. And - we no longer have to hear people remark that this is all new heresy, either, for it has a very ancient background.

Similarly, it is much safer for a fundamentalist to believe that the Bible as it exists today was dictated as such by the finger of God, even though the King James version is not as accurate a translation of the ancient texts as one can get, and even though Shakespearian English did not exist 2,000 and more years ago. And, the fundamentalist reader will believe our accounts when we speak of things which they consider to be evil, but are grossly ignorant as to their true purport. Then we get rocks thrown at us, when we attempt to show, that what has been considered evil throughout the centuries, is actually not evil at all, and in fact is the legitimate truth, and that which has been considered good is the real heresy, intended for the slaves to follow to their hearts' content.

So, when we speak of Pagan connections, Gnostic survivals and the like, we (and those that we are really writing this material for) see Triumph, Praise, Truth. But when our adversaries see these things in print, they are convinced we are antichrists and that we are perverted, doomed, and damned.

Yet, they have had the blinds of ignorance (with the help of "saint" Paul and others of his ilk) controlling all that they see, hear, or think, like the Control Voice on The Outer Limits. And their ministers, or shepherds, control the vertical as well! But - we can see in all we have researched, and all that we present here, a pattern that goes way back as far as we can reckon, and spreads from Morocco, Spain and the British Isles east as far as China, Korea, and Japan. When we add the "New World" to the mix, we can add North , Central, and South America as well, and while we're at it, the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans, too.

They got up and Zee guided him to the metro station, where he explained to NuNew how to navigate through Paris. NuNew took out his phone and noted the advice. 

“We have to go to the thirteenth arrondissement first. It’s the Asian Quarter of Paris, and they sell Sangkhathan baskets there. From there, we will go to Bois de Vincennes, where la Grande Pagode is.” 

NuNew nodded and let himself be guided by Zee, who looked like he had everything planned out. 

The trip was nice, and Zee kept giving NuNew advice and sharing restaurant recommendations, which was great, but it also made NuNew dread the moment the day ended, because that meant that Zee would be gone, and he’d be alone in the city again. 

After they purchased the basket, it was time to travel to Vincennes. For some reason, NuNew was feeling nervous. The last time he had made merit was a decade ago for Songkran, when he met his fiancé, and he was afraid that he had forgotten the steps for entering the temple.

He fidgeted nervously with his fingers while bouncing a leg and kept repeating the steps. Lighting the candle, leaving the flower, lighting the incense, taking his shoes off… 

Zee’s voice blurred into the background noise as his anxiety grew. This was important to him, and yet, he felt like he was going to do something wrong. For a moment, he had the urge to tell Zee that they should ditch the idea and go back home, but when he tried to speak, he couldn't form the words. 

They arrived at their destination, and Zee confidently got up and led the way out of the train. NuNew followed behind, having to double the pace to catch up with him. 

The Pagode was in a beautiful place, surrounded by nature. The faint smell of incense mixed into the air helped him relax a little bit as he followed Zee towards the temple, but still, everything was in a blur.

All he knew was that he was with Zee, and that was it. 

“NuNew, I asked if you were ready.” Zee said, his brows knitted together in what seemed to be concern. 

“I can’t do this. I don't remember how to. It’s been way too long.” 

Zee’s features softened and a warm smile appeared on his face as he took NuNew’s hand. “Follow my lead. I happen to make merit very often.” 

NuNew copied everything Zee did, although he felt like an impostor that was about to offend his own culture. But Zee was very attentive, and kept whispering in his ear what the next step was. 

When they were in front of the monk, a new wave of anxiety took over him. He knelt down on the carpet, at a respectful distance, and bowed three times until his forehead touched the floor. Then, Zee handed him the basket and NuNew held it out with shaky hands. 

“Venerable Father, I’d like to offer a Sangkhathan and ask for my best friend’s health and speedy recovery.” He said, his voice trembling with nervousness, but also a deep sadness as he thought of Kat. 

The monk gave NuNew a gentle, compassionate nod and gestured towards the floor between them. NuNew leaned forward and placed the golden basket on the carpet.

BELAS KNAP: A NEOLITHIC MONUMENT THAT MAKES YOU MOVE

Belas Knap is one of the great Cotswold-Severn long barrows, but photographs rarely prepare you for the experience of actually walking around it.

At first, the great stone façade appears to offer an entrance.

It doesn’t.

The imposing portal is a false entrance.

To reach the dead, you have to move around the monument and find the separate chambers opening from its sides. The architecture controls your approach, redirects your body and changes what you can see as you move.

That is what fascinates me about these places.

They were not simply containers for burials. They were carefully constructed encounters between stone, landscape, architecture, the living and the dead.

But Belas Knap makes much more sense when you actually move through it.

🎥 Come with me around the monument and see what the photographs miss. Watch the full Belas Knap film on YouTube:

https://t.co/zV2yjnwVlm

What does the monument make the body do?

Look closely. Think independently. Keep the wonder.

text:
Return to Nicodemus. Having witnessed the miracle at Cana, the cleansing of the Temple, and Jesus’ powerful teaching, he was clearly stirred, yet still fearful, which is why he came at night. Imagine him hearing Jesus refer to Moses and the bronze serpent, and then saying, “So must the Son of Man be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life.”
The title “Son of Man” comes from the Book of Daniel (7:13–14), in which the prophet sees the “one like a son of man” coming on the clouds of heaven to receive everlasting dominion. Jesus used this title frequently to describe Himself, linking His earthly mission with divine authority.
In His encounter with Nicodemus, Jesus veils the deeper meaning. His being “lifted up” refers not to earthly power, but to His Crucifixion. Nicodemus likely didn’t grasp this at the time. He may have assumed Jesus was foretelling a messianic rise to political rule, overthrowing Roman oppression. Only after the Crucifixion and Resurrection would Nicodemus—and the other disciples—begin to understand the true nature of this first revelation that the lifting up of the Son of Man was the lifting of the Cross, the source of healing, life, and eternal glory.
Today, we are invited to exalt Christ’s Cross in our own souls. The paradox of the Cross—that such brutal torture and death brings life—is our glory. Because of Jesus’ Cross and the saving power that flowed from it, every suffering we endure, every cross we carry, and every injustice we suffer has the potential to share in the Exultation of the Holy Cross if we allow ourselves to be lifted up with Him, in confidence and rejoicing.
Reflect today on the mystery Jesus first revealed in secret. Through His exaltation on the Cross, He brings salvation to all who believe, also enabling our crosses to share in His triumph. Gaze upon the Cross with faith. What once symbolized death has become our hope, our healing, and our path to eternal life.
Most highly exalted Lord, though You spoke in veiled language when revealing Your “lifting up” to Nicodemus, You later spoke clearly as You offered Your life on the Cross for the salvation of the world. I pray that You and Your perfect Sacrifice may always be exalted in my heart—first through gratitude and praise, and then through imitation. Lift me up in every cross I carry, so that You may continue to be exalted through my life for the world to see. Jesus, I trust in You.

An excerpt from ‘Catholic Daiy Reflections’

text:
Kevin Garnett says a vacation in Jamaica turned into a frantic trip home after he opened a copy of USA Today and learned that his agent had rejected a massive contract offer from the Minnesota Timberwolves without his approval.

"I'm in Jamaica... I never forget this. I got the USA Today. I pop it open, dog. The first thing, it says, 'Garnett denies $122.' And I'm like, what the [expletive]? Sat up, like, what the [expletive] happened? I had a bowl of food in my lap, and I remember spilled on the [expletive], and I was like, what the [expletive]? Tap shorty, come on, got it, we got to go. And I zoomed home, right.

"And the problem was I never got to deny anything. You know, the agent did. So, firstly, I checked him was about, 'Hey look, don't be speaking for me.'... And I was like, 'No,' so I ain't really like that, so I fired him."

That detail does not line up with reporting from 1997. Garnett remembers seeing $122 million in the newspaper, but contemporary reports placed Minnesota's rejected six-year offer at roughly $102 million to $103.5 million, suggesting he may be misremembering the figure nearly three decades later.

Garnett's frustration centered on the decision being made without him. He said his agent had turned down the offer and spoken on his behalf without his approval, prompting him to fire the agent and become more involved in the business side of his career.

Minnesota later increased its offer to $120 million before Garnett ultimately agreed to a six-year, $126 million extension in October 1997, a record-setting contract at the time.
